title: The Dragon’s Followers
text: After that, my Father warned the man who appeared to be the representative of the eastern village that if they didn’t dispose of the dragon’s carcass soon, things might get serious. However, the man didn’t seem very responsive. Eventually, we set off in a hurry… but since Filolial-sama and the others were reluctant to put Gaelion in the carriage, and Gaelion himself refused to get in, he ended up walking along behind us.
“Aren’t you going to make Wyndia-chan my slave?”
“Well, she has her own free will… It’d be better for her to become one if she wants to get stronger, but what do you want to do?”
The assistant is keeping quiet. She looks a bit hesitant, but I wonder what to do.
“Actually, there’s something I want to ask Wyndia.”
“What?”
“From now on, we’ll be fighting monsters to make Wyndia and Gaelion stronger, but I’d be in trouble if you told me you didn’t want to hurt monsters…”
“Why would I need to say something like that?”
“Huh? But you were raised by a dragon, right?”
“It’s survival of the fittest among monsters—my dad used to say that, too. He said it’s necessary to survive and get stronger.”
“Ah… so that’s how you see it. Well, I guess I can rest easy then. Even if it comes down to it, there are plenty of ways to avoid becoming a slave…”
“Since you’re so kind, big bro, I’d actually feel safer as your slave, you know?”
“Hmm…”
“It’s different from Keel-kun’s situation, after all… Besides, Keel-kun doesn’t have to be a slave either, right?”
“It’s fine! Actually, thanks to this, I feel like Big Bro is protecting me right now!”
Keel proudly shows off his slave mark.
“I’m glad you’re proud of it, but—”
“Oh, really?”

“Yeah. Well, there are plenty of other things I can do, like boosting your potential… You’ll be fine even if you don’t become a slave. I can always just cast a protective spell on you as a ‘masked slave’ whenever I want.”
“Yes.”
“Then, Wyndia, you don’t have to become a slave… Besides, you wouldn’t want to be a slave to an acquaintance of the Hero who killed your father, would you?”

The assistant fell silent and looked down. It seems she still harbors a desire for revenge. In this case, wouldn’t the slave mark actually be necessary to prevent her from doing anything reckless? That’s what I think, but since it concerns your Father, I’m sure he has his reasons, so I, Motoyasu, remain silent.
“……Well.”

My Father cut off the rest of what he was about to say. After all, the target of her revenge would be far too inconvenient for us. While our goal is to stop her, it would be best to keep the Assistant’s reckless behavior in check.
“Gau!”
“As for Gaelion-chan… you should bind her with a monster mark. Make sure… the two of you—one person and one beast—grow stronger together.”
“Gau! Gau gau!”
“Huh? So you’re going to become the Shield Hero’s monster… too?”
“Gau!”
The monster the assistant was leading let out a cry, and the assistant said to my Father.
“Huh? Shouldn’t you register Wyndia-chan as your master…?”
When my Father asked again, the monster cried out once more.
“I want to get stronger… and also, since the Shield Hero helped me, I want to repay him for that…”
“Gau!”
The monster is asserting itself while jumping up and down. Sakura-chan watches this with a displeased look and, as if to make a point, wraps her arm around her Father’s arm.
“Sakura-chan?”
“I’m not giving Naofumi up.”
“Gauuuu!”
It feels like their gazes are clashing with a crackling intensity. Father and the Assistant watch the scene in bewilderment.
“A-anyway… so shall Naofumi and Wyndia handle Gaelion-chan’s master registration? Is that okay?”
“Y-yeah.”
The Assistant nods, looking troubled, while Sakura-chan and the monster continue their staring contest.
After that, we finished disposing of the food we’d grown on the Lazy Pig’s territory without any issues. So, we’re heading back to the Lazy Pig’s parents’ territory to load up again.
“Oink…”
Thanks to the Lazy Pig’s connections, we called in a merchant who could handle monster registration, and my Assistant’s monster was officially registered as a monster under human command.
“Well then… for now, let’s focus on leveling up Wyndia and Gaelion. I haven’t seen much of Lars-chan lately, either.”
Just as my father muttered that,
“…I don’t want to raise a dragon’s offspring.”
“I don’t want to.”
“No way.”
“Piyo!”
“I don’t like dragons either.”
Filolial-sama and the others—and I—all refused. Naturally, we were completely ignored. My father looked exhausted.
“Sigh… I knew you guys didn’t get along, but…”
“Big bro! I’m in!”
“Yeah, I think I’ll ask Keel-kun to help out. Luna-chan… are you going to stay home?”
“Piyo…”
“Boo…”
“Elena-san, that’s not right. Don’t look so blatantly annoyed…”

Scratching his head with a troubled look, my Father mumbled, “Crunch, crunch.” I might be willing to go a hundred paces to help level up my Assistant, but leveling up a dragon’s minion? Not on your life.
“Anyway, for now, Sakura-chan will stay behind, and we’ll head to Siltvelt for some secret leveling.”
“Huh? I have to stay behind?”
“You don’t want to, do you?”
Sakura-chan muttered under her breath with a look of deep distress, and Father replied.
“Well then… I don’t want to, but I’ll put up with it.”
“Piyo…”
“Gau! Gau gau!”
“Mmm!”
Once again, Sakura-chan and the monster were locked in a staring contest. The Assistant watched the scene and tilted her head in confusion.
“Siltvelt?”
“Ah, that’s the name of a country far away from Melromarc. Don’t you know about it, Wyndia-chan?”
“I only know what my dad tells me… I don’t know anything about the human world.”
“I see… Since you were raised by a dragon, Wyndia-chan, you only know a monster’s standards, huh?”
“…Yeah.”
“Let’s learn about the human world little by little, okay?”
Seeing that the Assistant isn’t responding, Father gently places a hand on her shoulder as if to teach her.

“It’s easy—and maybe even comfortable—to think only about the monster world. But… you’re going to have to experience the human world from now on. Ignorance leads to death. Monsters with little experience get killed by outside enemies in the blink of an eye, don’t they?”
“Yeah. I know that because Dad told me so.”

“What you’re about to learn is the human world… I think it operates on a different set of common sense than the monster world. But it’s the same in that showing weakness or being ignorant can put your life in danger. From now on, I want to teach you all sorts of things so you can survive in the human world, too.”
“Gau!”
The monster let out a cry to the Assistant. The Assistant then nodded as if in agreement.
“Yeah, I get it. I’ll study so I don’t get taken down.”

“That’s a good answer. If you learn the common sense of the human world, you might be able to avoid losing. You might be able to use your wits to defeat strong opponents. You might even be able to protect your loved ones from people who resort to underhanded tactics. Do your best.”
“So, how do we get to Siltvelt?”
“Um, well… Yuki-chan. Could you stop pulling the carriage for a moment?”
“Certainly.”
The carriage came to a stop.
“Yuki-chan, since the others don’t want Gaelion-chan in the carriage, could you at least put her in the one that isn’t being pulled?”
“Mm.”
When the Assistant beckoned, the monster hopped right into the carriage. What’s going on here? The carriage is going to start smelling.
“We’re going to teleport to Siltvelt, but what about you, Motoyasu-kun?”
My Father already has a portal. It’s the usual method, isn’t it?
“Do I really need to go too?”
Since my Father is already strong enough, I think it’d be fine if we all went our separate ways. After all, I have to make the accessories my Father asked me to make.

“I can go, but on the way back, if Motoyasu-kun doesn’t use his concealment magic, people will find out I’ve been flying around and doing all sorts of things… So either way, we’ll have to arrange a meeting spot, won’t we?”
“No problem at all. I’ll come pick you up at the agreed-upon time. I was planning to head to the mine anyway today to make that accessory.”
“Oh, really? Then come pick me up when evening rolls around.”
“Understood.”
“Well then, I’m off. Portal Shield!”
My father, Sakura-chan, Keel, Luna-chan, the Assistant, and the monsters all vanished in a flash.
“Well then, I’ll keep an eye on things while Father is away, and we’ll be on our way.”
“Yes, ma’am.”
Yuki-chan resumed pulling the carriage.
“Oink…”
The Lazy Pig started snoring calmly even amid the jostling. Just how unmotivated is this thing?
“What are we going to do about the Kitamura accessories?”
“First, we’ll go to the mine using the letter of introduction we got from the Lazy Pig’s parents, Yuki-chan.”
I stuck my head out of the carriage and showed Yuki-chan the map. It’s not like I don’t know the way, but it’s always better to let Yuki-chan know as well.
“Well then, let’s get going.”
“Here we go!”
Yuki-chan pulled hard on the carriage and started racing along.
